name: Disorder of Bilirubin Metabolism and Excretion

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Bilirubin Metabolism Disorders

criteria.description: Persistent elevation of unconjugated or conjugated serum bilirubin levels beyond normal reference ranges
Abnormal liver function tests indicating impaired bilirubin conjugation or excretion
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in bilirubin metabolism (e.g., UGT1A1 mutations)
Exclusion of hemolytic causes of hyperbilirubinemia through hematological evaluation
Histopathological evidence of impaired bilirubin conjugation or canalicular excretion abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent elevated serum bilirubin with abnormal liver function tests and exclusion of hemolysis; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic of disorders like Gilbert syndrome and Crigler-Najjar syndrome
searchTerms: persistent high levels of unconjugated bilirubin

pathognomonic.notes: Yellow discoloration of skin and sclera due to bilirubin accumulation

searchTerms: high levels of conjugated bilirubin in blood

common.notes: Excretion of conjugated bilirubin in urine
searchTerms: bilirubin in urine causing dark urine

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic liver dysfunction

common.notes: Enlarged liver due to metabolic dysfunction

occasional.notes: Itching related to bile salt accumulation
searchTerms: skin itching due to liver problems

occasional.notes: Common presentation in newborns with bilirubin metabolism disorders

occasional.symptomName: Transient neurological symptoms (kernicterus in severe cases)
occasional.notes: Rare but severe complication in unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia
searchTerms: temporary neurological symptoms from bilirubin toxicity
transient brain symptoms in severe jaundice

rare.notes: Occurs in untreated Crigler-Najjar syndrome type 1
searchTerms: severe brain damage from high bilirubin
blood clotting problems due to liver failure

rare.notes: Progressive liver damage due to impaired bile flow
searchTerms: liver scarring caused by bile flow blockage

laboratory: Elevated serum unconjugated and/or conjugated bilirubin
Abnormal liver function tests (elevated ALT, AST, ALP, GGT)
Normal hemolysis markers (reticulocyte count, LDH) in non-hemolytic cases
imaging: Ultrasound may show hepatomegaly or biliary tract abnormalities
Liver biopsy demonstrating impaired bilirubin conjugation or canalicular cholestasis
genetic: Mutations in UGT1A1 gene (Gilbert syndrome, Crigler-Najjar syndrome)
Variants in genes affecting bilirubin transport and excretion
other: Response to phenobarbital therapy in some conjugation defects

distinguishingFeatures: Absent or abnormal bile ducts on imaging
Failure to thrive and pale stools

references: Mayo Clinic Proceedings. Disorders of Bilirubin Metabolism. 2022.
Orphanet Report Series. Bilirubin Metabolism Disorders. 2023.
